role: Exports a finished Emuqu workout HRVSession to HealthKit as an HKWorkout via HKWorkoutBuilder, with per-tick heart rate (opt-in, not Apple-sourced), distance and net active-energy sample series placed on the wall clock around pauses, pause/resume workout events, and an optional GPS route. Every object it saves carries the session's identity as ExternalUUID and sync identifier with the export's sync version; an export first finds what earlier exports of the session saved (by identity, or a legacy copy by its start second) and deletes what HealthKit did not replace once the new copy is saved. When Health refuses that read because the phone is locked, the workout is saved anyway and the session is noted (PendingWorkoutReplacements) so the next foreground backfill deletes every copy but the newest. Also deletes a session's exported workouts when the session is deleted forever.
types: HealthKitWorkoutExport: enum — namespace of static export/removal + pure sample builders
HealthKitWorkoutExport.ExportStamp: struct — session id + sync version; the identities and metadata of the workout, its route and its samples
HealthKitWorkoutExport.EarlierExport: struct (@MainActor) — an earlier export's workouts and the samples/routes saved with them; find, match, delete
HealthKitWorkoutExport.SampleOptions: struct — body weight + which series to write

WorkoutWallClock: struct — start date + pause spans sorted by atElapsed; maps active (pause-excluded) seconds to wall-clock Dates, tick intervals that never span a pause, and pause start/resume moments
PendingWorkoutReplacements: enum (@MainActor) — the sessions whose workout was saved while Health could not be read, by session id with the start time; note/clear/finish
state: ud:hkPendingWorkoutReplacements ([uuidString: startDate seconds since 1970]; PendingWorkoutReplacements.key, swept by Delete All My Data)
toplevel: Constants for the ACSM kcal formula and the resting MET. After the enum, the file-scope @MainActor enum PendingWorkoutReplacements (its UserDefaults key) and the struct WorkoutWallClock (stored startDate and sorted pauseSpans, no other top-level code).

units.does: Saves a finished workout session to HealthKit, replacing earlier exports of it: requires workoutMetadata and endDate and workout write authorization; finds the earlier exports (EarlierExport.findUnlessLocked: nil when the phone is locked, any other read failure throws); builds and finishes an HKWorkout under a fresh ExportStamp with the sample series sampleOptions chooses; attaches the GPS route (none for a HealthKit-sourced session); then deletes what the earlier exports saved, keeping objects whose sync identifier the new export reused (HealthKit replaced them), and logs success (replaceEarlier). Saved while the earlier exports could not be read, replaceEarlier notes the session for the next backfill (PendingWorkoutReplacements.note), logs, and deletes nothing. Throws ExportError, builder, query or delete errors to the caller; a failed delete throws after the new workout is saved.

units.does: After an export saved the session's workout: deletes what the earlier exports saved except the objects whose sync identifier is in `keeping` (HealthKit replaced them) and logs the saved workout with its sport, duration and how many earlier workouts it replaced. With no earlier exports read (the phone was locked), notes the session for the next backfill (PendingWorkoutReplacements.note), logs, and deletes nothing. Delete errors propagate.

For a session deleted forever: finds every workout the app exported for it (EarlierExport.find from the recording's start) with the samples and routes saved with each, deletes them all, and drops the session from the pending locked-save cleanups (PendingWorkoutReplacements.clear); logs how many workouts went. Without HealthKit it does nothing; lookup and delete errors propagate (the pending entry then stays).

units.does: Builds delta-distance samples for sports with a Health distance type: ticks sorted by offset, each increase over the last cumulative distance becomes a sample spanning from where the previous written delta ended (the workout start for the first) to this tick, so a delta that built up over non-advancing ticks covers all of them, each with the stamp's 'distance' sample metadata numbered in the order written. The span is placed on the wall clock by clock.interval(fromActiveOffset:to:), so it never crosses a pause: one a pause interrupted starts at that pause's resume.

Builds per-tick active-energy samples from net METs (netMETs: gross Compendium METs less the 1 MET of rest, floored at 0): kcal = netMETs × 3.5 × bodyWeightKg × minutes / 200 over the active seconds since the previous tick (since the workout start for the first tick), skipping non-positive/non-finite METs and windows ≤ 0.01 kcal, each with the stamp's 'energy' sample metadata numbered in the order written. Each sample is placed on the wall clock by clock.interval(fromActiveOffset:to:), so it never crosses a pause (one a pause interrupted starts at the resume).

branches.effect: window starts at the previous tick; the first tick's window starts at the workout start (a tick at offset 0 still gets max(1,0) = 1 s)

units.does: Wall-clock Date of an active (pause-excluded) second: start + offset + the lengths of every pause that began before it (a tick at the second a pause began maps to the pause start). Same rule as WorkoutMetadata.wallClockSeconds(forActiveOffset:).

Wall-clock (start, end) of a quantity built up between two active seconds. End is date(atActiveOffset: end). When a pause began in [start, end) the interval starts at the last such pause's resume (end moment minus the active seconds after that pause), so it never spans a pause and the amount from before the pause is put after it; otherwise it starts at date(atActiveOffset: start).

branches.effect: returns (date(start), date(end)); otherwise starts at the last such pause's resume

units.does: Each pause as wall-clock (start, end): start = start date + atElapsed + the lengths of the pauses before it in order, end = start + its length; pauses at the same active second follow one another.
